citation.title: Björk-Jarabak Cephalometric Analysis: Posterior/Anterior Ratio, Sum of Angles

curation.notes: accessed 2026-10-07 (both extractors read the live page that day). onfile page 'Updated March 27, 2026'; [source removed] Dental page (no date shown) for #44 only, accessed 2026-10-07. onfile names Jarabak & Fizzell (1972) and Björk's original growth studies as its sources. Merge 2026-10-08 (Re-read with WebFetch on 2026-10-08, onfile 15:17 and [source removed] 15:18): #35, #36, #37, #38, #39, #40, #42 definitionMatch a 'same' / b 'close' -> close: the page defines gonion as constructed, the catalogue uses the AI's anatomical Go. #44 a 0.75 ([source removed]'s '~3:4' ideal, no SD) / b 0.799 ± 0.063 ([source removed]'s table, 79.9 ± 6.3 %) -> 0.799 ± 0.063 (merge-notes ruling; the table row is the printed norm, the '~3:4' is a rounded ideal). #43 b only (1.0, [source removed]'s '~1:1') -> omitted (merge-notes ruling: [source removed]'s table gives only the inverse ratio; see caveats). Every value re-read on the onfile page matched both extractions. Sources: b's row-specific wording.

caveats: Website values, not from a paper (status website; never coloured).
onfile's table has a column headed 'SD'; its ± values are stored as sd. Its 'Clinical Range' column is given in each entry's note.

onfile defines gonion as a CONSTRUCTED point (ramus tangent × mandibular-plane tangent; re-read 8 Oct). The catalogue's ruling C3 says 'onfile uses Go' and the app uses the AI's anatomical Go, so every entry that uses gonion is 'close'. The catalogue's C3 sentence needs correcting.
#37 upper gonial, #38 lower gonial and #42 Jarabak ratio: onfile prints the 'Mean Norm' as a band (52°–55°, 70°–75°, 62%–65%) with no SD; stored as range, the wider clinical range in the note.
#40 S–Go and #41 N–Me: onfile prints '~80 mm' and '~122 mm' (approximate) and says the clinical range is 'Sex/age dependent', with no separate values by sex or age.

#43 cranial base to body (S–N ÷ Go–Me): no website norm. onfile gives none; [source removed]'s table gives only the inverse, Go′–Me/S–N = 111.2 ± 6.3 %, and a rounded ideal '~1:1'. Omitted rather than inverted.

#44 posterior cranial base to ramus is from [source removed] Dental's 'Analysis Data (Jarabak)' table, not from onfile (onfile's page gives no value for it). [source removed] does not say which sample the table comes from.

Not in the catalogue ([source removed]): S–N 66.0 ± 3.4 mm, Ar–S 37.2 ± 5.2 mm, Ar–Go′ 46.3 ± 5.2 mm, Go′–Me 73.4 ± 4.9 mm. [source removed]'s angles and S–Go′/N–Me differ from onfile's; onfile's are entered, as briefed.
